intro: Lesson 37: Flowers, pollination and seed dispersal. To understand how flowering plants make seeds and spread them

picture.draw: Draw and label: Flower diagram and seed dispersal cards

blocks.title: Sort into: Wind / Animals / Water / Bursting pod
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Wind, Animals, Water, Bursting pod.
blocks.answer: Wind: Dandelion; Sycamore. Animals: Blackberry; Burdock hooks. Water: Coconut. Bursting pod: Pea pod

cards:
pollination
moving pollen from the stamen
to the stigma

pollen
a yellow powder made by the
stamen

stamen
the male part of a flower that
makes pollen

stigma
the sticky top of the female
part that catches pollen

dispersal
spreading seeds away from the
parent plant
blocks.task: use them to test yourself or a partner.

questions.q: Burdock seeds have tiny hooks. How are they dispersed?
questions.a: They hook onto animal fur and are carried away
questions.model: Look at the feature: hooks. What do hooks catch on? Fur. So animals carry them: animal dispersal.

questions.q: Which part of a flower makes pollen?
Look at a flower (from a garden or supermarket) or the photo. Draw and label petal, stamen, stigma and ovary.
questions.a: Labelled drawing with the four parts
questions.model: Teacher draws a simple flower on camera and labels the stamen: 'makes pollen'.

questions.q: Design a seed that would be dispersed by wind. Explain its features.
questions.a: Light with wings or fluff to catch the wind

questions.q: Why do wind-pollinated flowers (like grasses) not need bright petals?
questions.a: They do not need to attract insects

questions.q: Moving pollen to the stigma is...
Big question: why should a seed land far from its parent?
questions.a: To get its own light, water and space.
